- Added `challenge_target_distance_mi` and `challenge_target_elevation_ft` to `PlannerConfig`.
- Passed these values through relevant functions to `write_plan_html` and `export_plan_files`.
- Implemented calculation and display for:
  - Progress % (for new official distance/elevation vs. target)
  - % Over Target (for total on-foot distance/elevation vs. target)
  - Efficiency Score (target vs. total on-foot distance/elevation)
- Updated `AGENTS.md` to include these new challenge objectives, example statistics, and definitions for the key evaluation metrics.

These changes provide better tools for evaluating the generated challenge plans against specific goals.

Forces dnf to be the package manager of choice for openscap remediations that modify packages for bootc / image mode machines.

author: reuterbal
body:
Pull request #563 highlighted a potential design flaw in our handling of Transformation entry points in transformations for items that define their own scope (in some sense) but are not program units, more specifically the transformation entry points for typedefs or interfaces. Currently, the scheduler “applies” the transformation to `Item.scope_ir`, which usually refers to the `Module` or `Subroutine`. But for `TypeDef` and `Interface` it points to the `Typedef` or `Interface`, which is then silently ignored in a `Transformation.apply` (i.e., even when including these in the processing, they wouldn’t incur any changes to be applied).

So far, we didn’t have any transformations that needed to transform either of them itself, thus this wasn’t a problem. But the analysis pass in #563  requires this now.

The underlying cause for this is that `scope_ir` is meant to provide the scope of an item, in which any definitions are declared - which is, e.g., used to figure out where definitions like `ProcedureBinding` are anchored. Until now it just happened to also coincide with the suitable transformation entry point in relevant cases so far.

My proposal to work around this is to introduce instead a separate `transformation_ir` property on items to explicitly declare for an item the entry point for transformations. In most cases this will be an alias for `scope_ir` but with specific overloads for `TypeDefItem`, `ProcedureBindingItem` and `InterfaceItem`. This will ensure a consist entry point behaviour.

I have slightly amended the tests for `TypeDefItem` to verify this behaviour on top of the implicit testing via asserting correct behaviour of transformations. I suspect test coverage might point out a few blind spots, though, which I will close with another commit.

3) Moved open nodes to a priority queue that stores them based on their f value for faster f value look up. (No more harsh sorting)
4) Added a sightline check to optimize clear paths performance.
5) Optimized heuristic calculation which increased performance on all paths.
6) Fixes #4884

- title: "Update notes (8.6 to 8.7)"

+ To upgrade Optimize to version 8.7, perform the steps...
